To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) we propose a learning-to-ranks approach to entity ranking that uses a set of features that are extracted from web documents, entity mentions and the knowledge base; ii) our best system achieves a MAP of 0.35 on TREC Web13 data and of 0.38 on TREC Web14 data; iii) our best system is competitive with the state-of-the-art on TREC Web data and outperforms all other methods on TREC Robuste04 data.

(i) the combination of different features that relate entities to the query, document mentions and knowledge bases, is crucial for entity retrieval; (ii) single features like the frequency of entity mentions within the top ranked documents, and the score of entities in the knowledge base against a query, are generally good indicators for entity ranking; and (iii) entity retrieval performance is comparable with document retrieval, but the latter is more robust and reliable, since it is based on a well-established and mature technology.

i) entity ranking is a challenging task, which requires a combination of features that relate the entity to the query and the document; ii) the performance of the best features is comparable to the performance of the state-of-the-art document ranking systems; and iii) the performance is still far from being perfect, thus indicating that there is still room for improvements.
